question: Why can glass be recycled almost forever?
answer: Glass does not degrade when it melts, so a kilogram of waste glass becomes a kilogram of new glass. That makes the yield almost 100%, and the loop can repeat round after round. The page lets the reader drag to see how much is left after each melt.
move: Melting doesn't wear glass out, so the loop barely loses anything.

web.label: A long glass furnace with eight glowing mouths, one per melt; at the start a green bottle holding 1 kg of old glass, and over each melt the faint outline of a full bottle. The reader drags across to stand a bottle over each melt as tall as the glass they think is left, then says how sure, and sees a kilogram of waste glass become a kilogram of new glass.

source: Geopop, “Il processo di riciclo del vetro” (YouTube, 2021)
